children: Shares of Shadowfax Technologies Ltd. are in focus on Wednesday, November 25, after the company said it is acquiring WeFast (Borzo India) for ₹23.3 crore.

The company said the deal marks its entry into the on-demand intra-city goods transportation, which is one of the largest logistics markets in India and one that is formalizing fast. It also opens a significant new growth engine, extending Shadowfax's services to small and medium businesses and customer-to-customer deliveries.

WeFast was founded in 2016 in Mumbai and has earned a following among small businesses and C2C users to move goods across their city quickly. It now operates in over five cities, where more than 32,000 delivery partners complete over 1.2 crore deliveries a year, Shadowfax said. WeFast has generated roughly ₹200 crore in adjusted revenue in the calendar year 2025, it added.
Shadowfax Tech listed the following strategic rationale for the acquisition of WeFast:
Large market at the start of its digital shift:
SMEs and C2C users are embracing online platforms for transparent pricing, on-demand vehicles and real-time tracking, and the organized segment is growing at more than 50% a year.
Bringing enterprise-grade logistics to SMEs and C2C users:

Through the WeFast app, shopowners, distributors and individuals can get the same reliability and technology that larger platforms in the country get from Shadowfax, it said. They can book two, three and four-wheelers on demand for urgent intra-city deliveries with upfront pricing and live tracking.

Launched in FY26, Shadowfax 360 opened the company's express parcel network to SMEs and D2C brands and crossed 6,700 transacting sellers within two quarters. WeFast takes the same model form parcel shipping to intra-city goods transportation, the company said.
Scaling nationwide on Shadowfax's technology and network:

Shadowfax said it brings the reach to scale WeFast as it has move 3.8 lakh delivery partners across more than 16,000 pin codes. Shadowfax said with WeFast it can now serve the entire spectrum of customer needs, from express parcel to hyperlocal deliveries and on-demand itnra-city goods movement.
Intra-city goods transportation is a natural adjacency to Shadowfax's hyperlocal business, which grew revenue 87.7% from last year to ₹341 crore in the second quarter, the company said.
Shares of Shadowfax Technologies ended the previous session 1% lower at ₹304.25 apiece. The stock has risen 6.5% in the past month.

title: Shadowfax Tech shares in focus on WeFast acquisition to enter intra-city logistics market
